string.text: .45 calibre magazine with a bullet, whose design remains popular for over a hundred years. It is a heavy round with a relatively small gunpowder load that has low velocity, but considerable stopping power.

Custom tooled .45 ACP ammunition - jacketed hollow point bullets with steel cores. This combination is peculiar, as it has advantages and shortcomings of both armour piercing and hollow point ammunition types.
Standard 12 gauge shell filled with lead shot, 6mm calibre. Immense stopping power and mayhem at close ranges. Only for smooth bore shotguns.
A 12 gauge shell with a single, large bullet. Typically used for big game hunting, it can be used for other purposes. The round doesn't quite pierce body armour, it literally punches through them.
Military magazine, 5,45 x39 mm 7N22 armour piercing bullets. Widely used in Warsaw Pact automatic rifles. Bullets have a carbide core, effective against body armour.

Military magazine, 5,45x39mm 7N10 enhanced penetration bullets. Widely used in Warsaw Pact automatic rifles. Reduced recoil and increased range result in greater accuracy compared to older 7,62mm rounds.
NATO 5,56x45 mm armour piercing rounds, designated SS190/M855. Effective against body armour. Widely used in small arms, armies and intelligence services of Western countries.
Standard light NATO magazine of 5,56x45mm bullets, designed for maximizing effectiveness of burst fire. Designation SS109. Excellent ballistic characteristics.
Specially designed 7,62mm sniper rounds. Bullet's steel core gives improved ballistic performance and better armour piercing than standard bullets of the same calibre.
Cheap standard 7,62mm rounds. The design and feed system make them useless as sniper rifle ammunition, but perfect for the RPD machine gun.
Standard 9x18mm bullet with a steel core and lead filling under a metal jacket. Good stopping power, but useless against body armour.
European marking + P + indicates a higher gunpowder load, increasing the velocity of the round by one third, giving it better stopping power against unarmoured targets.
Standard 9x19mm bullet magazine. Good ballistic performance and low price led to its widespread use. Ineffective against body armour.
Hollow point bullet with an expanding top has great stopping power and doesn't bounce. Typical police and civilian self defence ammunition. Ineffective against body armour.

Subsonic SP-6 ammunition has a hollow point and a partially open core of hardened steel. Silencer required to maximize it's potential for silent fire. Popular in Warsaw Pact countries. Performs well against body armour.

Subsonic "sniper" ammunition SP-5 is covered by a bimetallic shell, with the cavity behind its steel core filled with lead. Silencer required to maximize it's potential for silent fire. Popular in Warsaw Pact countries.
40mm M209 grenade. Effective blast radius is about 5m. Compatible with FN 2000's integrated grenade launcher.
RPG-7 anti-personnel grenade. With the launcher it can destroy an enemy hiding at distances beyond the reach of a hand grenade.
Ammunition for the GP-25 Bonfire, OC-14 Storm and the RG-6. Effective blast radius is about 5 m.
A standard Soviet scope with fixed 5x magnification and a scale for determining distance to the target. Can be mounted on most Warsaw Pact weapons that use the Dovetail rail.
A 5x scope with a built-in thermal imager, allowing for easy acquisition of human targets. Widely used by special forces. Can be mounted on most Warsaw Pact weapons that use the Dovetail rail.
A low light scope with 5x fixed magnification. Designed for combat in the absence of light sources. Can be mounted on most Warsaw Pact weapons that use the Dovetail rail.
A military scope with range finder and adjustable zoom (1.6x to 4x) with the possibility of self-regulation to improve accuracy. Mounted on a Picatinny rail.
Fixed magnification 4x scope. Most commonly used in small arms to improve accuracy on medium and long ranges. Mounted on a Picatinny rail.
A low light SUSAT scope with fixed magnification (1.6x). Designed for close combat in low light conditions. Mounted on a Picatinny rail.
A 4x scope with an integrated night vision device. Designed fir night time long range combat. Mounted on a Picatinny rail.
A fixed magnification 1.6x scope. Designed for short and medium range combat. Mounted on Picatinny rail.
A fixed magnification (2.7x) scope, optimized for medium range combat and urban warfare. Can be mounted on most Warsaw Pact weapons that use the Dovetail rail.

An universal silencer kit, easily adaptable. The inside of the barrel is surrounded by a roll of fine brass mesh and several chambers, all designed to reduce noise and mask flame when the weapon is fired. Includes a set of adapters and seals for common calibres.
A standard hand grenade; its shrapnel can penetrate medium bulletproof vests and wound targets in a radius of up to 7 m. Stalkers often appropriate them from the military.
A single-shot muzzle loaded grenade launcher for Warsaw Pact rifles. Automatic cocking system, with manual safety and automatic blocking if the weapon is improperly loaded. Uses VOG-25 grenades.
A modified single-shot Gewehraufsatz 97 grenade launcher with a shortened three inch barrel and a Picatinny rail adapter. Due to its universal nature, it's widely used worldwide.
An offensive hand grenade with a small blast radius of about 5 m. It is often used to clear out mutant burrows.
A smoke hand grenade. Designed to deploy a smoke screen within ten seconds of deployment.

A cut down regular hunting rifle with horizontal twin barrels, much more compact and lightweight than your typical shotgun. Commonly used by bandits, as it's easily concealable and effective in close quarters.
An unique pistol, based on a regular Desert Eagle. Parts fit each other with incredible precision, giving it unprecedented accuracy in fire fights.

A bull pup automatic rifle with an integrated grenade launcher, the Storm borrows 3/4 of its internal mechanics from the AK-74. Despite utilizing a different calibre (9x39mm), layout and upgrade ability, it's every bit as reliable as its uncle. Initially designed for rapid response military units, it enjoys popularity with soldiers and stalkers alike, thanks to its ability to safely destroy enemy armour and cover.
A prototype Russian modification of the OC-14 Storm system, designed specifically for military operating in the Zone. Easily identifiable by the increased magazine capacity.
A modified model of a pistol from the first half of the 20th century. Despite its age, its still highly popular worldwide.

This sub machine gun has a popularity that is well deserved, as it's reliable, easy to use and highly accurate. When it was phased out by police and military units in favour of newer models, it appeared in large quantities on the black market and, eventually, in the zone.
Experimental sub machine gun, developed on the basis of a regular MP5. It was built as the next generation close combat weapon, with an extreme rate of fire and high accuracy.
This gun belonged to Zulus, who increased the cassette size and designed a special ejection mechanism. The modification increased the weapon's weight, but for him it was not a problem.
A special Makarov pistol, awarded to Degtyarev for successes in high-risk assignments, valour and courage. So says the engraving.

An automatic grenade launcher, with a revolver-like drum magazine loaded with six VOG-25 grenades. Designed to engage entrenched enemies and provide cover fire, it's every bit as useful when attacking highly protected facilities or particularly nasty critters.
The ammo belt feed was modified manually. Despite the weight and low accuracy, this weapon is quite popular in the Zone, both as a suppressing fire tool and mutant sweeper.
Limited edition SIG P220, created in small numbers for an undisclosed customer. It's characterized by an increased magazine capacity, barrel of reinforced steel and polymer body.

First member of a new family of assault rifles. With high reliability, great accuracy and a comfortable design, it's one of the best weapons in its class. Not popular in the Zone due to its cost, although some have been bought by more experienced stalkers.

Obviously not a model straight out of the factory, this 550 is nevertheless in top condition, clearly its previous owner took good care of it. It is fully upgraded, with parts perfectly interlocked and working, giving a tremendous increase in killing efficiency. "S" is carved into the stock neatly, along with 16 small crosses.

Produced only in Duty workshops, this shotgun is made specifically for eradicating large packs of mutants. The feeding mechanism is modified to provide a high rate of fire, while the magazine capacity is increased to ten rounds. Uses 12x70 Gauge shells.
Basic SPAS-12, thoroughly modified for offensive units. Just like its "parent", its capable of fully automatic fire, though the recoil dampeners are much more effective.

This particular sniper rifle model was present on the arms market for over half a century, establishing itself a reputation as an exceptionally reliable, easy to use weapon. Intended as a military marksman's tool, stalkers appreciate it more for its ability to pierce even the toughest mutant hides and armour.
Assembled from Dragunov rifle parts, to the naked eye it seems no different than a regular rifle, but in reality, it has an even more impressive accuracy and destructive power.
Previously the prized possession of Max, Freedom's legendary leader, this rifle has an increased rate of fire, as it was meant to be a further development of the rifle.

Common hunting rifle. Twin vertical barrels provide it with sufficient accuracy and stopping power to keep monsters at bay, at least longer than with a regular pistol. Cheap and affordable in comparison with most other weapons, its popular with bandits and novices on the edges of the zone.
Looks like the internal mechanics are busted. One way or another, it's not going to work - even pressing the trigger doesn't do anything.
This pistol is quite popular among Zone veterans, thanks to its excellent accuracy and high reliability. Even certain drawbacks (such as size or cumbersome design) do not affect its popularity.
Apparently, this is a modified HK USP Compact pistol with an increased rate of fire. It seems it once belonged to Wolfhound, a mercenary leader.

A special military rifle with an integrated scope and silencer, designed for special operations marksmen, deployed on missions when stealth is key. High precision and firepower make it very popular with stalkers, even if its magazine capacity is lacking.
Based on the Vintorez, this rifle was designed specifically for military special operations. While the rate of fire was reduced, its firepower was significantly increased.

The definition of a western pump action shotgun, the 1300 enjoys widespread popularity in the Zone, thanks to its reliability and rate of fire. A corrosion resistant coating was applied to all parts of the weapon.
Former property of Tutsan, this custom made weapon was made according to the owner's main wish - to be able to put down hardy mutants with just one shot.

A modern military weapon, created to replace the aging AK-74. Its main feature is the ability to fire two round bursts with perfect accuracy at ranges of up to 100 meters. This fire mode greatly increases the chances of taking down a target with two, combined hits.

The Avtomat Kalashnikova Model 1974 became the main weapon of Warsaw Pact armies as they switched to smaller, higher velocity ammunition. Its large compensator reduces recoil, increasing precision and accuracy in all fire modes. On top of that, it's a simple, reliable weapon.

In terms of size and weight its a sub machine gun, but in terms of performance, it's basically a cut-down AK-74. Perfect for urban door-to-door warfare, when its small range and tendency to overheat are offset by its firepower.

A classic automatic weapon which served with distinction in all armed conflicts of the 20th century. Original and modified versions are produced to this day by tens, if not hundreds of manufacturers. Its only apparent drawback is a small magazine, but its offset by its firepower.

The definition of "hand cannon". Large, heavy and extremely powerful, it's perfect for sports shooting and hunting medium and big game. However, in the Zone it has had limited popularity, as it's also expensive and difficult to maintain in working condition.

This futuristic-looking weapon is a modular assault rifle of the 21st century. In this configuration, it has an integrated 40mm grenade launcher and a computer-assisted fire control module, on top of excellent ergonomics, great reliability and easy handling in all fire modes, despite its odd design.

An Ukrainian design, intended to succeed the PM as the sidearm of law enforcement and security agencies. Superior in all aspects to the Makarov, early models were unsuccessful among stalkers, as early production runs had horrible flaws. Nowadays, however, it is in quite a demand, thanks to new manufacturing technology, eliminating previously glaring flaws.

The G36 is the embodiment of next generation assault rifle technologies and design. Featuring a closed bolt with a delayed blow back system, it is a first class example of modern rifles: lightweight, durable and extremely ergonomic.

Early SA-80 rifles were horribly flawed and many found their way to the black market after decommissioning. From there, they arrived in the Zone, gaining popularity thanks to its integrated 4x SUSAT scope, highly accurate single shot mode and upgrade potential. A reminder: accuracy is non-existent in burst and automatic modes, on top of its tendency to jam when firing full auto.

A new generation of the famous family of rifles. Modifications to the receiver, barrel, ejection port and bolt mechanism resulted in improved reliability and ergonomics, in addition to, paradoxically, reduced weight. The end result is a highly accurate rifle, limited by its sensitivity to dirt and harsh treatment.

Created in the latter half of the 20th century from the Makarov Pistol, the PB was intended for intelligence teams and other covert personnel. While it's considered obsolete, in skilled hands it remains an effective weapon.

A legacy of the Soviet era, the Makarov Pistol is one of the best representatives of compact self defence weapons. Size, reliability and simple construction offset its relatively low firepower, accuracy and weight.

A smooth bore combat shotgun, designed to increase CQC firepower of military and police forces. It has a high magazine capacity and rate of fire, although size, mass and slow reloading limit its usefulness. A rare sight in the Zone, although it is used to clear out mutant packs.

Thousands of RPG-7s remained in military warehouses after the fall of the USSR, eventually ending up in the Zone. The RPG is a single shot, smooth bore recoilless launcher, designed in 1960. It has a fixed PS0-7 2.7x scope. Considerable size and weight make this weapon an uncommon sight, but its destructive power and ease of use did find several fans in the Zone.

The P220 is the latest SIG model and remains popular worldwide. This masterpiece of Swiss watchmakers has only a single drawback - small magazine capacity. Its excellent ergonomics, accuracy, firepower and reliability make it a popular choice for mercenaries and experienced stalkers.

A smooth bore automatic shotgun, the SPAS was developed in the latter half of the 20th century, as an universal weapon for police and military assault units. High reliability and tactical flexibility make it a popular anti-mutant weapon, despite its mass and price tag.

A more modern version of the SVD, this rifle was constructed in a bull pup layout. A higher fire rate, lower weight and a comparatively identical accuracy make its popularity among soldiers and stalkers well deserved.

Created from the ground up as a silent assault rifle for special operations, the Avalanche (rus: Val) is Vintorez's younger brother. The integrated silencer and 9x39mm heavy rounds allow the operator to engage armoured hostiles whilst remaining undetected.

An ultra high tech weapon, designated Product No. 62, this cannon was developed deep within the Zone by scientists working in secret laboratories. It bases its operation on a system of electromagnets, which propel the round to incredible speeds, giving it enormous penetrating power and virtually no recoil. For power, it uses parts of electric artifacts.

Pistols of this brand are recognized worldwide as reliable, if somewhat unwieldy. Widely used by militaries and policemen worldwide (and just as many criminals). As usual, models available in the Zone are not the most modern ones.

An excellent German pistol, with top-of-the-class ergonomics complimenting its other features, such as reliability or accuracy. Ever since their first appearance in the Zone, they became common sidearms of professionals and wealthy newcomers.
Energy cells powered by isolated shards of the Flash artifact, made in factory conditions with high tech equipment.
Primitive conditions and tools used instead of special equipment in production of this battery resulted in reduced capacity. The energy source is an isolated Flash artifact.
